subject: Post-call: FinWave discovery & model-fit + quantization tradeoffs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ethan Zhao <ethan.zhao@finwave.ai>, Priya Iyer <priya.iyer@finwave.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: FinWave discovery & model-fit next steps

Thanks for the time today — good discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move into a short eval: 

Recap:
- Use case: real-time financial risk scoring + occasional analyst-facing chat summaries. Primary goals: low token-latency for streaming (SLO target: median per-token latency <= 150ms) and high throughput for batch scoring (peak 800 qps batch).
- Data: short, structured prompts with dense numerical context + long tails for explainability. Concern: hallucination on out-of-distribution inputs.

Our recommended high-level approach:
1) Model candidates to evaluate (baseline -> production path):
   - Baseline: 13B FP16 (quality reference)
   - Throughput-first: 13B AWQ 4-bit (significant token/throughput savings, typically minimal quality delta on instruction-following tasks)
   - Quality-first / hardware-accelerated: 13B FP8 (requires H100/A100-class kernels; best quality retention, higher cost)
   - Alternative quantization: GPTQ 4-bit (can be better/worse depending on layer structure; we'll measure)

2) Evaluation plan (what we propose to run for you):
   - Side-by-side eval on your prompt set (attached finwave_prompt_set_v1.json) comparing FP16, AWQ-4, GPTQ-4, FP8.
   - Metrics: accuracy/precision on labeled examples, hallucination rate (manual sampling), latency P50/P95, and token cost estimates.
   - Duration: 48-hour run + summary. We'll provide a CSV of results (sample attached: benchmark_results_20260720.csv) and a short trade study (attached PDF).

3) Ask from you to start:
   - Share a representative 1-2k sample of anonymized prompts/inputs and (if available) expected outputs or labeling.
   - Confirm latency vs quality priority (you mentioned throughput is primary but wanted to balance hallucination risk).
   - Approve a brief NDA if you want results behind a partner contract; otherwise we can run a sandbox eval with redacted data.

Attachments: finwave_prompt_set_v1.json (prompt set), quantization_tradeoffs_AWQ_vs_GPTQ.pdf (short trade study), benchmark_results_20260720.csv (sample baseline numbers). Also linking our shared benchmark doc: https://drive.google.com/finwave-benchmarks

Next steps: can you confirm the sample data availability and preferred evaluation window? We can start as early as next Tue/Wed.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

- Latency: 150ms per-token target is aggressive — is that feasible with AWQ on our preferred cloud (we're on Azure NVads)?
- Can you give a rough ballpark of token cost delta between AWQ-4 and FP8 for the same throughput? Helps us budget before a formal eval.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: FinWave discovery & model-fit next steps

Thanks — great questions. Looping in Rishi (quant infra/pricing) and Laura (SE) to help with specifics.

Short answers up front:
- AWQ 4-bit: in our experience AWQ preserves instruction-following quality quite well on models with standard transformer blocks; we typically see 1-3% drop in automated metrics on instruction tasks, and subjective regression is often smaller but depends on prompt style. Hallucination risk typically increases slightly and should be measured via manual sampling (we include that in the eval).
- Latency on Azure NVads: AWQ often reduces kernel compute and memory movement which improves throughput and can reduce per-token latency vs FP16 when end-to-end I/O is not the bottleneck. FP8 has lower compute cost per op on supported HW but requires kernel support — if NVads don't have FP8 kernels optimized, AWQ can be the better practical path.
- Cost delta (very rough ballpark): AWQ-4 can reduce token compute cost by ~2-3x relative to FP16; FP8 sits between AWQ and FP16 in cost depending on kernel efficiency. We'll produce precise numbers from the eval.

I've attached the quantization trade study (quantization_tradeoffs_AWQ_vs_GPTQ.pdf) and an initial benchmark CSV so you can see expected latency/throughput ranges. Our recommended start: run the 48-hour side-by-side eval on your prompt set (we'll return both automated metrics and manual samples).

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) You share the 1-2k anonymized samples and any labels.
2) We schedule the eval window — prefer Wed/Thu next week.
3) If you want partner-level confidentiality we can sign an NDA; otherwise we'll run with data redaction.

If you confirm, Rishi can share the eval config and a quick cost/throughput estimate.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments: quantization_tradeoffs_AWQ_vs_GPTQ.pdf, benchmark_results_20260720.csv, finwave_prompt_set_v1.json

Subject: RE: Post-call: FinWave discovery & model-fit next steps (internal)

Internal notes / pricing + quantization playbook (summary for Marissa & Laura) — do not forward externally without redaction: 

- Eval configs to run (we'll produce per-config throughput and token-cost):
  A) FP16 13B baseline (reference quality)
  B) AWQ-4 (throughput-first) — expected 2-3x token throughput improvement over FP16 depending on batching; quality delta usually small for instruction prompts.
  C) GPTQ-4 (alternative 4-bit) — can be better for some weights/layouts, but results are model-dependent; include to validate AWQ results.
  D) FP8 (if available on customer's infra) — best quality retention; higher engineering/ops complexity and sometimes higher per-token cost if kernels are suboptimal.

- Performance knobs: enable KV-prefix caching for repeated user sessions, tune batch sizes (we'll sweep batch sizes up to their 800 qps target), and use continuous batching for latency/throughput balance.

- Cost estimates (very high-level): for their workload we expect AWQ to reduce GPU-token cost by ~55-70% vs FP16; FP8 could be ~30-50% lower than FP16 but depends heavily on kernel support and memory bandwidth. We'll provide a precise per-token estimate post-eval.

- Risk mitigations: run a small manual label set for hallucination-sensitive prompts, and implement a fallback policy that routes flagged prompts to FP8/FP16 models until the confidence filter is tuned.

I'll draft the eval config (exact instances, batch sizes, expected p50/p95) and share as soon as we confirm the data.

—Rishi
